div.div: Calibration: on the first workload EDF came within 1.1 ms [calc] of the work floor, so the owner densified it until placement (GPU 91 % [I11], DLA 0 % [I12]) became the lever
perception-chain metric, ms, as reported in note C3; densified rows are medians over seeds (8 px per ms)
perception-chain metric, ms, as reported in note C3; densified rows are medians over seeds (8 px per ms)

NOTHING TO FIND. EDF sits 1.1 ms [calc] above the floor and both units have slack (CPU 24 %, GPU 42 % [I5]). The baseline passes, the gate is calibrated, yet a campaign's ceiling is tiny: a passing baseline does not make a topic ready.

THE LEVER IS PLACEMENT. Dispatch order alone (EDF, least laxity) stays inside the baseline's range; earliest-finish placement moves work off the saturated GPU onto the idle DLA and the promoted candidate's median drops to 25.8 ms [I9]. Medians shown; promotion compares ranges (diagram 05).

HOW IT WAS DENSIFIED (on purpose, documented)
- a parallel segmenter in the perception chain
- a new depth-mapping chain
- several jobs made heavier
- control deadline set to 20 ms [I19]

A FAIR BASELINE, NOT A STRAWMAN
The first baseline placed jobs alphabetically: every accelerator job went to the DLA, perception reached 626 ms [I16] (off this scale) and the densified workload failed outright. It was replaced by shortest-execution placement: the default an engineer ships first.

GPU-GREEDY LOSES WHEN A LONG JOB BLOCKS THE GPU (diagnostic)
Held-out b, first calibration: GPU-greedy 37 ms vs CPU placement 29 ms [I17]. A 200 ms [I18] grasp-planner job holds the single non-preemptive GPU and perception queues behind it.

Legend: grey bar = baseline | green = best non-diagnostic policy | blue = other policy; dashed = diagnostic (did not pass through the frozen evaluator) | red = work floor (no scheduler beats it) | utilization: amber = before, green = after round 1, blue = CPU. Simulator output: illustrative, not a real platform.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (cited paper, or my arithmetic on public mathematics); [In] = illustrative (a design parameter of the harness, a round value that keeps the shape of the first campaign, or output of the demonstration scheduling simulator; never a measurement of a real platform); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/C3-calibration.md (two goals of calibration, work floor, densifying, baseline placement choice, GPU-greedy finding, round-1 result); notes/C2-the-scheduling-topic.md (platform, metric, held-out b). [calc]: 1.1 = 16.6 - 15.5. The first workload's DLA utilization is not in the notes and is not drawn.
